assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Continents or Pangaea, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Ba Trieu's single persona is planned here. The shape is Front-Load because every specialty district in the game must sit on a Woods, Rainforest or Marsh tile that exists at settle time; a Builder who chops the wrong tile or a Settler who plants on the wrong hex removes a district from the city for good.

verdict.one_line: Audit the features before every settle, pin a Theater Square on Woods, a Campus on Rainforest and a Thành on Marsh in each city before the first Builder arrives, chop nothing that is pinned, and let the terrain Culture plus the Thành's Tourism after Flight carry a Culture game nobody can invade.
verdict.why: Nine Dragon River Delta is a restriction with a yield attached: every building in a Woods district gives Culture, every one in a Rainforest district gives Science, every one in a Marsh district gives Production, so a Theater Square on Woods with three buildings is three Culture before adjacency. The Thành is an Encampment with no population requirement that gains Culture from each adjacent district and turns that Culture into Tourism at Flight, which makes the defensive district a Tourism source and every city a small fortress. Drive Out the Aggressors gives every Vietnamese unit fighting on Woods, Rainforest or Marsh +5 Combat Strength, so the army is small and the Production goes to Amphitheaters. Culture is the victory because the kit's late payoff is Tourism; Science is the fallback because Rainforest Campuses are the same decision made with the other feature; Domination is not here because the strength bonus needs a feature tile under the unit, and the Production goes to Culture.

must_have: At least four Woods, Rainforest or Marsh tiles in the capital's first two rings that are not resources, so the first three districts and a wonder have somewhere to sit.
Three more sites within ten tiles with the same count, confirmed by the Scout before the second Settler is produced.
prefer: Rainforest and Woods together: a Campus on Rainforest and a Theater Square on Woods in the same city gets both yields.
Marsh beside a river for the Thành, since Marsh is the one feature nobody else wants and the Thành cannot be adjacent to the City Center.
Hills under some of the Woods for Production; Vietnam builds many buildings and chops none of its own tiles.
Ha Long Bay or Pantanal in reach; both are feature tiles with Culture that the kit already wants to settle beside.
map_check.no_go: Open grassland, plains or desert with fewer than three feature tiles in the capital's first two rings and no forest or jungle visible within six tiles. Vietnam then cannot place a Campus or a Theater Square until Medieval Faires allows planting Woods, which is turn 100 on Emperor, and a civ with no districts for a hundred turns loses.
map_check.fallback: If features are visible but five or more tiles away, walk the Settler toward them for up to three turns and settle the first tile with three features adjacent. If nothing is visible by turn 4, settle in place for the Monument and the Warrior, send the first two Settlers to whatever forest the Scout finds, and treat the capital as a Holy-Site-free, district-free Gold city until Medieval Faires lets Builders plant Woods on its grassland; say plainly that the capital is the smallest city in the empire this game.

kit_levers.name: Drive Out The Aggressors
kit_levers.buys: +5 Combat Strength for Vietnamese units fighting on Woods, Rainforest and Marsh tiles, and extra Movement for units that start a turn on one.
kit_levers.exploit: The defence is the land: two Archers and a Warrior standing on forest tiles inside the border beat a Classical rush without Walls, and the Production saved goes to Amphitheaters. The army never leaves the trees; a Vietnamese unit on open plains outside the border is an ordinary unit, and the plan does not send one there.

kit_levers.name: Nine Dragon River Delta
kit_levers.buys: Specialty land districts can be built only on Woods, Rainforest or Marsh, and every building in such a district gains Culture on Woods, Science on Rainforest or Production on Marsh; Woods can be planted from Medieval Faires instead of Conservation.
kit_levers.exploit: District roles are assigned to features at settle time: Theater Squares and Holy Sites on Woods, Campuses on Rainforest, Thành and Industrial Zones on Marsh. The pinned tiles are never chopped, never improved and never given to a wonder. Medieval Faires is the recovery path: a city with no Woods gets one planted on grassland by a Builder and the Theater Square goes there.

kit_levers.name: Voi Chiến
kit_levers.buys: A Crossbowman replacement with extra Movement and Sight that can move after it attacks.
kit_levers.exploit: Four of them from Machinery are the whole Medieval and Renaissance army: fire from a forest tile inside the border, step back into cover the same turn, repeat. They hold the empire through the window when the Thành Culture is still Culture and not yet Tourism. They are not built to leave the trees.

kit_levers.name: Thành
kit_levers.buys: An Encampment replacement with no population requirement that cannot touch the City Center, gains Culture from each adjacent district, and after Flight produces Tourism equal to that Culture.
kit_levers.exploit: It is placed last in each cluster, on the Marsh or Woods tile that touches the most other districts, so the adjacency is the whole cluster. Every city gets one; the second-ring position keeps it out of the Theater Square's way. From Flight onward, six Thành at +3 or +4 Culture each are twenty-plus Tourism from a district that also holds Walls.

kit_levers.name: Defender of the Homeland
kit_levers.buys: Ba Trieu likes civilizations that have never declared war on Vietnam and never forgives one that has.
kit_levers.exploit: Irrelevant to your own play except as a reminder that an AI Ba Trieu on the map is a safe neighbour unless provoked; never declare a joint war that includes her.

turn_zero: Before the Settler moves: count the Woods, Rainforest and Marsh tiles in the first two rings of the start that carry no resource. Four or more is a go. Two or three: move one turn toward more features. Fewer than two with nothing in sight: run the fallback.

Before the Settler moves: note which features are which. One Woods, one Rainforest and one Marsh in the same ring is the ideal capital; two Woods and a Rainforest is fine; Marsh alone means a Production city and the Theater Square waits for Medieval Faires.

Before the Settler moves: pin the capital's cluster on the features. Theater Square on the Woods tile adjacent to the center, Campus on the Rainforest tile touching it, Holy Site on the next Woods, Thành on the Marsh or Woods tile in the second ring that touches two of the three. Nothing is queued in the capital on a pinned tile, and no Builder ever touches one.
By turn 10: audit every candidate site the Scout has seen the same way and write its cluster beside it. A site with fewer than three usable features is not a site, however good the river.
front_load.ceiling: Six to eight cities, each with three or four districts on features, each capped by the number of feature tiles its first two rings happened to hold. Culture around turn 270 on Emperor from Woods Theater Squares, Thành Tourism from Flight, Chichen Itza and Seaside Resorts or National Parks on the forest appeal, with Science close behind from Rainforest Campuses. The cap is districts per city, not population: a city that rolled two features has two districts forever unless Medieval Faires plants it a third, and the empire's total district count is the number the map dealt plus the Woods you plant after turn 100.

irreversibles.decision: Capital tile: it fixes which features are in the first two rings and therefore how many districts the capital can ever have.
Capital cluster pinned to features and the no-chop rule declared. A Builder who harvests the pinned Woods for a Settler removes the Theater Square.
The settle map with a terrain audit for cities two through six: each site's districts named on its features before the second Settler is produced.
Which feature in each cluster is the Thành; it cannot touch the center and it should touch the most districts, so it goes last and its tile is reserved first.
Which cities take the planted Woods at Medieval Faires. Builders plant one per charge, so the list of cities short a Theater Square is written before the civic lands.

front_load.settle_map_rule: Draw every city before the second Settler is produced. A site qualifies if its first two rings hold at least three Woods, Rainforest or Marsh tiles without a resource on them, and it is a strong site if one of each is present. Write the cluster on the map at settle time: Theater Square on Woods, Campus on Rainforest, Holy Site or Commercial Hub on the next Woods, Thành on the Marsh or on the Woods tile in the second ring that touches the most districts. Mark the pinned tiles as no-chop and no-improve. A site with a river and one Woods is skipped for a dry site with four; the river is Housing and the Woods is a district. Cities six through eight may be 40 turns away; they are audited now so that a Builder does not clear their Rainforest for a Farm at turn 50.

phases.name: Assess and commit
phases.objective: Settle among the features, pin the capital's cluster, declare the no-chop rule, audit and draw cities two through six, found the pantheon, and have the second Settler out and the Holy Site queued on its Woods by turn 20. The twenty turns that decide how many districts this empire will ever have.

build_order.why: Audits the sites the map drew: counts features at each candidate and finds the first civilization for Writing.
A second Warrior standing on a forest tile inside the border is worth a Spearman; it clears the one camp that shares the forest.
City two on the best audited site; the capital pays the population because Magnus is not yet available.
Culture is the plan's currency and the restriction slows the first district; the Monument keeps Early Empire on time.

First district, on its pinned Woods; State Workforce fires and the Shrine is the first Faith building. The Theater Square waits for Drama and Poetry.
City three on the next audited site; both satellites exist before the capital's second district.

A Slinger kill at the forest camp; one Archer per city is the floor.

Inspiration from the first Builder's three unpinned improvements; Ilkum.

policies.why: The pantheon by turn 22 before any Holy Site exists.

districts.note: First district, on its pinned Woods; the Theater Square needs Drama and Poetry, so the Holy Site comes first and every building in it gives an extra Culture.

pantheon.why: Holy Sites must sit on features anyway, and a Holy Site on Woods ringed by Rainforest takes a Faith per Rainforest tile; where the start is Marsh rather than jungle, Lady of the Reeds and Marshes turns the unpinned Marsh tiles into Production instead.

city_states.why: The first envoy is Culture in the capital toward Political Philosophy.

checkpoints.test: Capital settled with four or more feature tiles in two rings, its Theater Square, Campus, Holy Site and Thành tiles pinned to named features, and the Scout auditing sites?
checkpoints.pass: Continue; the settle map for cities two through six is written before the Settler finishes.
checkpoints.fail: Fewer than three features: run the fallback. Pins missing: place them this turn, before the Builder is built; a Builder with no pins chops a district.

checkpoints.test: Second Settler out toward an audited site, Holy Site queued on its Woods, the pantheon founded or one turn away, and cities two through six drawn with their clusters?
checkpoints.pass: Enter the delta phase and follow the map.
checkpoints.fail: No map yet: draw it this turn. Holy Site queued on a non-feature tile: it cannot be, the game refuses; if it is queued on the Rainforest meant for the Campus, cancel it and move it to the Woods.

tasks.text: Settle where four or more Woods, Rainforest or Marsh tiles without resources sit in the first two rings; move at most one turn to get there.
Pin Theater Square on Woods, Campus on Rainforest, Holy Site on Woods, Thành on the second-ring feature touching two of them; mark all four no-chop.
Scout every candidate site within ten tiles and count its features; write the count on the map beside it.
Draw cities two through six with each cluster named on its features; strike any site with fewer than three usable features.
Found Sacred Path, or Earth Goddess if the features are Woods on hills, or Lady of the Reeds and Marshes if the capital holds three or more Marsh.
Holy Site placed on its pinned Woods; the Shrine is queued behind it. The Theater Square waits for Drama and Poetry.

phases.name: Fill the delta
phases.objective: Settle cities two through six on the audited sites and place each cluster on its features in the pinned order: Theater Square, Campus, then the Holy Site or Commercial Hub, with the Thành tile reserved. Found a religion from two Woods Holy Sites so Faith buys Great Writers later. Low decision density; the work is following the map and not chopping.

checkpoints.test: Four cities on audited sites, a Theater Square on Woods in each, the capital Campus on Rainforest, no pinned tile chopped, and a religion in reach?
checkpoints.pass: Continue; cities five and six and the Thành.
checkpoints.fail: A pinned tile chopped: strike that district from the city and add the city to the Medieval Faires planting list. No religion in reach: buy the second Shrine and keep God King.

checkpoints.fail: Fewer than six cities: settle the rest before any wonder. Thành placed next to the center: the game refuses; place it on the second-ring tile reserved at turn 3.

tasks.text: Cities two and three settled on audited sites; Theater Square pinned on Woods in each and queued the turn Drama and Poetry lands.
Capital Campus placed on its Rainforest; Library queued for the terrain Science.

Capital Thành placed on its reserved tile once two districts touch it; Military Training collected.
Six cities on audited sites; write the list of cities short a Woods for the Medieval Faires planting.

phases.objective: The clusters finish: a Thành in every city, Universities on the Rainforest Campuses, Art Museums ready for Great Artists, Medieval Faires planting Woods in the cities that rolled none, and four Voi Chiến holding the forest. Nothing is built for war beyond them; the Thành and the trees are the defence.

build_order.why: Every city, on its reserved tile; Culture per adjacent district, and Tourism from Flight onward.

phases.name: Flight

Flight is the single most important tech this civ researches and it is taken out of order.

decision_triggers.name: A city has no Woods
decision_triggers.if: An audited site turned out to hold Rainforest and Marsh but no Woods, so its Theater Square has no tile.
decision_triggers.then: Put the Campus on the Rainforest and the Thành on the Marsh now, add the city to the planting list, and at Medieval Faires a Serfdom Builder plants Woods on the grassland tile reserved for the Theater Square. The city is a Science city until turn 110 and a Culture city after; say so and do not chop anything to fix it sooner.

decision_triggers.name: A neighbour marches in
decision_triggers.if: A rival army crosses the border before turn 150.
decision_triggers.then: Do not build Walls in the inner cities. Voi Chiến and Archers on forest tiles inside the border fire and step back; the Thành's own ranged attack finishes what they wound. Units that chase onto open plains lose the bonus and the fight.

decision_triggers.name: Builder about to chop
decision_triggers.if: A Builder is standing on a pinned Woods or Rainforest with Production or Food on offer for harvesting it.
decision_triggers.then: Move the Builder. The harvest is one Settler's worth of Production once; the district is Culture every turn for 250 turns. The only features ever harvested are ones outside every audited cluster.

decision_triggers.name: Culture outruns Science
decision_triggers.if: At turn 150 the civics tree is two eras ahead of the techs.
decision_triggers.then: Normal for this plan, except that Flight must not slip: beeline it. Slot Rationalism, or Natural Philosophy if The Enlightenment is not in yet, put Pingala on Researcher for twenty turns, and keep Culture first.

abort.trigger: Turn 80 with fewer than four cities on audited sites, or three or more pinned district tiles chopped so that the clusters cannot be completed before Medieval Faires.
actions: Stop settling sites that fail the audit; what exists is the empire, and the plan says so.
Play a generic Culture game from wonders and Great Works on whatever feature tiles remain: Apadana, Chichen Itza, Kilwa and the Hermitage in the capital, Faith-bought Great Artists.
Keep the Voi Chiến and the forest defence; the kit still makes Vietnam the hardest civ on the map to invade.

fail_state: Turn 150 with six cities of which three have no Theater Square because their Woods were chopped for Settlers at turn 40, Campuses placed on the one Rainforest that should have been the Thành, Flight unresearched, and Culture in the middle of the table. The placement decisions that caused it were made before turn 20 and no feature can be put back except by planting Woods one Builder charge at a time.
common_mistakes: Harvesting a Woods or Rainforest for the Production. For any other civ it is a free Settler; for Vietnam it is a district removed from the city for the game unless Medieval Faires replants it a hundred turns later.
Placing the Thành adjacent to the City Center. The game refuses, and the player then puts it on the Woods meant for the Theater Square; its tile is the second-ring feature reserved at settle time.
Settling for the river. A river gives Housing; a Woods gives a Theater Square with a Culture bonus on every building. The audit counts features, not water.
Treating the strength bonus as an offensive kit. It applies only on Woods, Rainforest and Marsh; an army that marches out onto open ground is ordinary and the Production it cost was an Amphitheater.
Reaching the Industrial era and spreading research across the tree. Flight switches the Thành to Tourism; it is the first Modern-era tech this civ takes, every game.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset with the New Frontier Pass (Vietnam, Ba Trieu, Thành, Voi Chiến, Nine Dragon River Delta, Drive Out the Aggressors).

Where the civ-info text is thin, the game is followed: the district restriction applies to specialty districts only, so Neighborhoods, Aqueducts, Dams, Canals and Spaceports may sit on any legal tile; the building bonuses are +1 Culture on Woods, +1 Science on Rainforest and +1 Production on Marsh; the Thành cannot be adjacent to the City Center and has no population requirement; Vietnam plants Woods from Medieval Faires rather than Conservation.
